probes.query: Where is the per-target namespace name set to N_AVX3 (the macro that selects the AVX3 SIMD namespace)?
expectedFacts: set_macros-inl.h defines HWY_NAMESPACE to N_AVX3 in the AVX3 branch, which is the per-target inline namespace code is emitted into for that target
probes.author: cpp-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n 'define HWY_NAMESPACE N_AVX3$' hwy/ops/set_macros-inl.h -> hwy/ops/set_macros-inl.h:380 (#define HWY_NAMESPACE N_AVX3). Sibling targets N_SSE4/N_AVX2/etc defined nearby.

probes.query: Find the tag alias that describes a vector with EXACTLY kNumLanes active lanes (a power of two), even on scalable-vector targets — the one you'd use instead of CappedTag when you require exactly that many lanes.
expectedFacts: FixedTag<T, kNumLanes> is a using-alias that resolves to detail::FixedTagChecker<T, kNumLanes>::type, where the checker static_asserts kNumLanes is non-zero and does not exceed HWY_LANES(T)
probes.author: cpp-author
probes.notes: hard_for_tools: the public symbol is a one-line template using-alias (template <typename T, size_t kNumLanes> using FixedTag = typename detail::FixedTagChecker<T,kNumLanes>::type) whose actual logic lives in a separate detail:: struct with non-type template params; the constraints (static_asserts) are in the checker, not the alias. Verified: grep -n 'using FixedTag' hwy/ops/shared-inl.h -> shared-inl.h:423; grep -n 'struct FixedTagChecker' -> shared-inl.h:367.

probes.query: I want the function-pointer typedef for the custom abort handler that SetAbortFunc installs — where is the AbortFunc type declared? I looked in abort.h and found nothing useful.
expectedFacts: AbortFunc is typedef'd in base.h as void (*)(const char* file, int line, const char* message); abort.h is an empty compatibility header that explicitly states all Abort/Warn functionality lives in base.h
probes.author: cpp-author
probes.notes: hard_for_tools / header misdirection: abort.h is empty except a comment 'All Abort/Warn functionalities are in base.h' (hwy/abort.h:9), so a tool anchoring on the abort.h filename finds no symbol. The real typedef is in base.h. Verified: grep -n 'typedef void (\*AbortFunc)' hwy/base.h -> hwy/base.h:322; grep -n 'All Abort/Warn functionalities are in base.h' hwy/abort.h -> hwy/abort.h:9.

probes.query: How does the public VectorBytes() entry point get the actual lane count for the CPU's chosen target at runtime? Trace it to the per-target implementation it dispatches to.
expectedFacts: The public hwy::VectorBytes() calls HWY_DYNAMIC_DISPATCH(GetVectorBytes)(), and GetVectorBytes — defined inside the per-target namespace HWY_NAMESPACE (e.g. hwy::N_AVX3) — returns Lanes(ScalableTag<uint8_t>())
probes.author: cpp-author
probes.notes: hard_for_tools: caller and callee share the file but the callee GetVectorBytes lives inside 'namespace HWY_NAMESPACE' (the target-specific namespace, e.g. N_AVX3) compiled once per target, while the public VectorBytes is in plain hwy:: under #if HWY_ONCE; the link is the HWY_DYNAMIC_DISPATCH macro, not a direct call. Verified: grep -n 'size_t VectorBytes' hwy/per_target.cc -> per_target.cc:60 (public, returns HWY_DYNAMIC_DISPATCH(GetVectorBytes)()); grep -n 'size_t GetVectorBytes' hwy/per_target.cc -> per_target.cc:35 (inside namespace HWY_NAMESPACE at per_target.cc:32). Public decl per_target.h:40.

probes.query: Where is the dynamic-dispatch table index for the current CPU chosen, and what resets that selection mask from the set of SupportedTargets()?
expectedFacts: ChosenTarget::Update (in targets.h) stores the selection mask via StoreMask(HWY_CHOSEN_TARGET_SHIFT(targets) | scalar fallback), and SupportedTargets() (in targets.cc) calls GetChosenTarget().Update(targets) after DetectTargets() so GetIndex() yields the dispatch-table slot
probes.author: cpp-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n 'struct ChosenTarget' hwy/targets.h -> targets.h:341; void Update(int64_t targets) at targets.h:345; GetIndex() at targets.h:362; grep -n 'HWY_DLLEXPORT int64_t SupportedTargets' hwy/targets.cc -> targets.cc:811, which calls GetChosenTarget().Update(targets) at targets.cc:823 after DetectTargets().

probes.query: Where is the aligned-allocation entry point AllocateAlignedBytes declared versus actually implemented? I need both the public declaration and the definition.
expectedFacts: AllocateAlignedBytes is declared HWY_DLLEXPORT in aligned_allocator.h and defined in aligned_allocator.cc, where it over-allocates, stashes an AllocationHeader, and returns an aligned payload pointer
probes.author: cpp-author
probes.notes: Header/impl split. Verified: grep -n 'void\* AllocateAlignedBytes' hwy/aligned_allocator.h -> aligned_allocator.h:58 (declaration); hwy/aligned_allocator.cc -> aligned_allocator.cc:69 (definition, HWY_DLLEXPORT void* AllocateAlignedBytes(const size_t payload_size, ...)).

probes.query: The allocator deliberately staggers allocations to avoid cache aliasing (everything landing at the same address mod 2K). Where is the cyclic alignment offset computed for that?
expectedFacts: NextAlignedOffset returns a cyclic offset that is a multiple of kAlignment, advancing an atomic counter mod kGroups (kAlias/kAlignment) so successive allocations are staggered to reduce cache aliasing on x86
probes.author: cpp-author
probes.notes: Behavioral (why, not just where). Verified: grep -n 'size_t NextAlignedOffset' hwy/aligned_allocator.cc -> aligned_allocator.cc:57; comment 'Returns a random (cyclical) offset for AllocateAlignedBytes' at :56; uses atomic next.fetch_add % kGroups (:62), kAlias rationale comment at :40-42 ('aliasing can only occur at multiples of 2K').

probes.query: How does highway install a user-provided abort handler in a thread-safe way, and what does the install function return — does swapping the handler hand back the previous one?
expectedFacts: SetAbortFunc stores the handler via AtomicAbortFunc().exchange(func), which atomically swaps in the new handler and returns the previously-installed AbortFunc
probes.author: cpp-author
probes.notes: Behavioral. Verified: grep -n 'AbortFunc SetAbortFunc' hwy/abort.cc -> abort.cc:62; body 'return AtomicAbortFunc().exchange(func);' at abort.cc:63; AtomicAbortFunc() wraps a function-local std::atomic<AbortFunc> at abort.cc:30-31.

probes.query: Where does highway offload SIMD kernels to the GPU (CUDA / OpenCL device code)?
probes.author: cpp-author
probes.notes: Verified absent: grep -rin 'cuda|__global__|cudaMalloc|opencl|gpu' --include=*.h --include=*.cc hwy/ -> 0 results. Highway is a CPU SIMD abstraction (SSE/AVX/NEON/SVE/RVV/WASM); it has no GPU/CUDA/OpenCL offload path. Agent must confirm the negative.
